From: Lauren Mitchell <lauren.mitchell@britannia-bank.com>

Cc: security_ops@britannia-bank.com
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Evidence request: residency, retention, and proof-of-deletion for EU data

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our SOC/compliance team has a few follow-ups specifically tied to data residency and deletion controls before we move to final sign-off. Could you provide:

1) A TTL/residency mapping document that shows where customer data (including backups and snapshots) is stored by region and the retention TTL for each data class (tokens, logs, customer artifacts).

2) A sample deletion/audit trace showing a full tenant lifecycle deletion: request -> job run -> KV/cache purge -> backup snapshot removal (or retained backup policy) -> KMS key rotation/logs. We need enough detail to validate irreversible deletion for GDPR purposes.

3) Confirmation of S3/bucket replication behavior for EU customers (are replicas in EU only or cross-region?).

We'd like to have these artifacts by EOD Tue (UK time) to feed into our SOC 2 assessor. Feel free to redact anything sensitive; we mainly need timestamps, job ids, and the retention policy text.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick screen-share tomorrow if helpful.

--
Lauren Mitchell
Senior Manager, Information Security
Britannia Bank

Attaching the audit slice and a short readme inside the zip (redaction applied). Summary below to save time for the assessor:

- Deletion request received: 2026-09-28T08:42:11Z (request id: del-7f8a2)
- Deletion job scheduled: 2026-09-28T09:00:00Z (job id: job-3b4c)
- KV/Cache purge completed: 2026-09-28T09:00:17Z
- Main object store deletion API call recorded: 2026-09-28T09:00:21Z (s3-object-delete-event id: ev-9c2d)
- Snapshot pruning job removed related snapshot: 2026-09-28T09:10:05Z (snapshot-id: snap-88a)
- Backup retention policy check: backups retained for 30 days for short-term customer snapshots; longer-term archived snapshots are retained per customer's contract and require separate removal request (we explicitly document archive retention in the TTL mapping PDF).
- KMS entry logged for key access during deletion: 2026-09-28T09:00:20Z (kms-log id: kms-44f)

Notes on irreversibility: our standard deletion flow removes application-layer objects and triggers snapshot pruning. For cloud provider-level backups, we maintain a documented retention window; when backups are removed we also zero out associated metadata and (for encrypted objects) rotate and retire keys where applicable to reduce recoverability risk. For customers requiring immediate removal from backups, we provide an elevated archival-purge process that we execute under SOC-approved runbook with audit logging (this is typically a contracted add-on).

Attachments included: sample-deletion-audit-slice-20261005.zip (contains sanitized logs, job traces, and readme).

Thanks — the timeline is helpful. Two quick clarifying Qs from our assessor after reviewing the artifacts:

1) For archived snapshots retained beyond 30 days, can you confirm the default replica locations? We need to ensure any archived copies for EU customers remain within EU jurisdictions unless the customer explicitly opts-in to cross-region replication.

2) In the sample logs, we see a KMS access event and a key id. For the scenario where a customer requests accelerated purge of backups, can you outline the steps and approx SLA (we'd expect a documented runbook and a target completion window so the assessor can mark control effectiveness).

If you can answer those two points in one short email, that will probably close our assessor's questions.

--
Lauren

Hi Lauren — answers below (copying short bullets for the assessor):

1) Archived snapshot replica location (default):
- Default: archived snapshots for EU tenants are stored in EU-only regions (we pin replication to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 based on tenant region). Cross-region replication only occurs when explicitly enabled by customer contract (opt-in). We will include the relevant policy excerpt in the TTL PDF.

2) Accelerated purge runbook & SLA (outline):
- Step 1: Customer submits elevated purge request via support portal with business justification (creates ticket).
- Step 2: Security/ops validate request and escalate to Data Lifecycle Runbook owner (SLA: ack in 4 hours during business days).
- Step 3: Run elevated archival prune job that explicitly targets archived snapshots and triggers object delete + metadata zeroing (estimated execution: 2–8 hours depending on dataset size).
- Step 4: Post-run KMS actions: retire/rotate keys associated with the archived data if encryption keys are customer-scoped (logged in kms-rotations audit).
- Step 5: Deliver confirmation package to customer (job ids, timestamps, retained log slice) and update ticket (target confirmation window: 24–48 hours end-to-end for typical cases; very large archives may take longer).

We've attached the TTL mapping PDF and the sanitized audit slice per your original ask. If the assessor needs a short video walk-through of the runbook or a signed attestation from our Security team, we can schedule that for Wed.

Thanks — let us know if that finishes the ask.

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
